mainTopic: Whether צפור means only kosher birds, what 'טהורות' excludes in the מצורע's birds, and שילוח הקן when the eggs or chicks are not fit to eat
overview: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק's rule that the תורה's word צפור means only a kosher bird. A פסוק in דניאל is turned aside, because non-kosher birds are only called 'birds of the heavens.' 'כל צפור טהורה' is explained as pointing to a kosher bird that is still forbidden: the slaughtered bird of a מצורע, whose eating breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה. Next come two proofs from the מצורע's 'two living kosher birds.' 'Living' is read as having whole limbs. 'Kosher' cannot be about a טריפה, because the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל already excludes that. So four אמוראים give the word a new job: רב נחמן בר יצחק says birds of an עיר הנדחת, רבא says reusing a bird before it is sent away, רב פפא says birds traded for idol birds, and רבינא says a bird that killed a person. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה: a kosher bird sitting on non-kosher eggs is exempt from שילוח הקן because of רב כהנא's rule, 'take for yourself, and not for your dogs.' Finally, it asks why a טריפה mother is not compared to טריפה chicks; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse in דניאל that seems to call all birds 'צפרי'
steps.stepSummary: The challenge quotes דניאל, where 'צפרי' dwell in a tree's branches. Every kind of bird does that, so the word seems to include non-kosher birds too.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in its branches will dwell the birds of the heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge against רבי יצחק by quoting a פסוק in דניאל that uses the word 'צפרי' for birds sitting in a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All birds, kosher and non-kosher, sit in tree branches. So if the פסוק calls them 'צפרי,' the word צִפּוֹר would seem to cover non-kosher birds too. That goes against רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds (Aramaic plural of צִפּוֹר)
Its branches

phrases.english: 'And in its branches will dwell the birds of the heavens'
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:9

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that צפור means only a kosher bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every type of bird sits in branches, so 'צפרי' here must include non-kosher birds.

steps.title: Non-kosher birds are called 'birds of the heavens,' not plain 'birds'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that non-kosher birds only get the name 'צפרי' together with the extra word 'שמיא.' Plain 'צפרי' still means kosher birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are called 'birds of the heavens'; they are not called simply 'birds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from דניאל. The full phrase there is 'צפרי שמיא,' not just 'צפרי.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added word 'of the heavens' makes the name broader. Without that word, plain צִפּוֹר still means only kosher birds, so רבי יצחק's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain, unspecified (with no extra description)
They are called

phrases.english: They are called 'birds of the heavens,'
but they are not called plain 'birds.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the פסוק in דניאל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק uses the longer phrase 'צפרי שמיא,' not plain 'צפרי.'

steps.title: 'Every kosher bird' suggests some birds are not kosher
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge. The תורה says 'כל צפור טהורה,' every kosher bird, so there must also be a non-kosher צפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Every kosher bird [you may eat].' Doesn't that imply there is also a non-kosher one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רבי יצחק from a פסוק in דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צִפּוֹר always meant a kosher bird, the word 'טהורה' (kosher) would be unnecessary. Adding it seems to show that a non-kosher צפור also exists.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from the wording you can infer
Kosher (here: a bird that is allowed to be eaten)
Non-kosher (a forbidden species)

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'Every kosher bird [you may eat]',
phrases.notes: דברים 14:11

phrases.english: which implies that there is a non-kosher one?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that צפור means only a kosher bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Describing a צפור as 'טהורה' implies that some צפור is not טהורה.

steps.title: It implies a kosher bird that is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'טהורה' does not point to a non-kosher species. It points to a kosher bird that is still forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It implies that there is a forbidden one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge by reading the implication in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every צפור is a kosher species. But some kosher birds are still not allowed to be eaten for other reasons. 'Every kosher bird you may eat' excludes those, not non-kosher species.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden (to eat), even though it is a kosher species

steps.confusionAlert: 'טמאה' (a non-kosher species) and 'אסורה' (forbidden for some other reason) are not the same thing. The answer depends on that difference.

phrases.english: No, it implies that there is a forbidden one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the פסוק implies a non-kosher צפור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The implication could be about a kosher bird that is forbidden, not a non-kosher species.

steps.title: Which forbidden kosher bird is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kosher-but-forbidden bird this could be. Both options it tries are already taught elsewhere, so the inference seems to teach nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? If it is a טריפה, that is written outright. And if it is the slaughtered bird of a מצורע, that comes from the end of the פסוק: 'And these are what you shall not eat of them' includes the slaughtered bird of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer in step 4 by asking which bird it means. It shows that both obvious options are already covered by other פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה bird is already forbidden by an explicit פסוק. The slaughtered bird of a מצורע is already forbidden by the next part of this same passage. So 'כל צפור טהורה' would seem to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
The bird slaughtered in the purification of a מצורע (a person with צרעת)
Openly, explicitly
To include (a case learned from the פסוק)

phrases.english: What is it?
If it is a טריפה, that is written explicitly!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:8 already says not to eat a נבלה or טריפה.

phrases.english: And if it is the slaughtered bird of a מצורע,
that is already learned from the end of the פסוק:
'And these are what you shall not eat of them,'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:12

phrases.english: which comes to include the slaughtered bird of a מצורע.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kosher-but-forbidden bird the פסוק 'כל צפור טהורה' is excluding, given that both candidates are already taught elsewhere.

steps.title: It is the מצורע's bird, adding a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק really is about the slaughtered bird of a מצורע. What it adds is that eating it also breaks a positive commandment (עשה), on top of the prohibition (לא תעשה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about the slaughtered bird of a מצורע, and the point is that one transgresses both a positive commandment and a prohibition for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 5 by showing that the פסוק does add something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Every kosher bird you may eat' implies you should eat only permitted birds. So eating the forbidden one also breaks a positive commandment. The end of the פסוק already gives the לא תעשה, so the two together make two violations.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (keeping the first option after all)
A positive commandment
A negative commandment, a prohibition

phrases.english: Really, it is about the slaughtered bird of a מצורע,
and it teaches that one transgresses a positive commandment and a prohibition for it.
phrases.notes: The positive commandment comes from 'you may eat': eat only permitted birds. The prohibition comes from 'you shall not eat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a new job: adding an עשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to repeat the prohibition on the מצורע's bird, which is already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: It adds a positive commandment, so eating the bird breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Why not say it adds an עשה for a טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The same answer would also work for a טריפה: say the פסוק adds an עשה to that prohibition. Why choose the מצורע's bird?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us apply it to a טריפה, and say one transgresses a positive commandment and a prohibition for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 6. It asks why the extra עשה should go to the מצורע's bird and not to a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה also has a clear prohibition, so the 'add an עשה' idea fits it just as well. The גמרא needs a reason to prefer the מצורע's bird.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us apply it (explain the פסוק as being about a certain case)

phrases.english: But let us apply it to a טריפה,
and say one transgresses a positive commandment and a prohibition for it?

steps.kashyaTarget: The choice in step 6 to apply the פסוק to the מצורע's bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning fits a טריפה, so there is no clear reason to prefer the מצורע's bird.

steps.title: The context is slaughtered birds
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק is understood through its context. This passage is about properly slaughtered birds, so it fits the מצורע's bird, which was slaughtered, and not a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A matter is learned from its context, and this is written in the context of a slaughtered bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 7 with the rule that a פסוק is explained by its surroundings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses around 'כל צפור טהורה' talk about birds that were slaughtered and could be eaten. The מצורע's bird was properly slaughtered and still is forbidden, so it matches that context. A טריפה does not fit as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter learned from its context (a rule for reading פסוקים)
The topic or context of the passage

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק's rule stands: plain צפור means a kosher bird. 'כל צפור טהורה' points to a kosher bird that is forbidden, the slaughtered bird of a מצורע. Eating it breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and we know which bird is meant from the context of slaughtered birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule of reading a פסוק by its context (דבר הלמד מעניינו) being used to pick between two possible readings.

phrases.english: It is a matter learned from its context,
and it is written in the context of a slaughtered bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק by its context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra עשה could just as well apply to a טריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The passage is about slaughtered birds, so it refers to the מצורע's slaughtered bird.

steps.title: A proof from the word 'living' in the מצורע's birds
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the מצורע needs 'two living birds.' The גמרא suggests 'living' means 'permitted to eat.' That would imply some צפרים are not permitted, meaning non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Two living birds.' What does 'living' mean? Doesn't it mean living in your mouth, that is, allowed to be eaten? Then we can infer that some birds are not allowed to be eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the פסוק about the מצורע's birds. The proof is meant to show that some birds called צפור are non-kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds are obviously alive, so the word 'חיות' seems to add something. The proof reads it as 'fit to eat.' If the תורה has to say 'fit to eat,' then some צפרים must not be fit to eat. That would contradict the claim that every צפור is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: birds; the word whose scope is being tested
living
'living in your mouth': permitted to eat
by inference; from the fact that this was said

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'Two living birds,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:4, about the birds used to purify a מצורע.

phrases.english: what does 'living' mean?
Is it not that they are living in your mouth?
phrases.notes: He means birds you are allowed to eat.

phrases.english: By inference, there are birds that are not living in your mouth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the inference from 'כל צפור טהורה' was explained away, the גמרא tries a new פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That some birds called צפור are non-kosher
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'חיות' in ויקרא 14:4, read as 'permitted to eat'

steps.title: 'Living' means the limbs are whole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'חיות' means the birds have all their limbs. It does not mean 'permitted to eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'living' mean? That the tips of their limbs are alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving the word 'חיות' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חיות' still adds a requirement, but it is about the bird's body. A bird missing a limb cannot be used. Nothing here tells us about non-kosher species, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: the ends or tips of the limbs

phrases.english: No. What does 'living' mean?
That the tips of their limbs are alive.
phrases.notes: The limbs are still attached and whole, not cut off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of 'חיות' as 'permitted to eat'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'חיות' can mean having whole limbs, so it implies nothing about non-kosher birds

steps.title: A proof from the word 'kosher' in the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק says the birds must be 'טהורות.' That seems to imply some צפרים are טמאות, meaning non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the end of the פסוק: 'kosher.' Doesn't that imply there are non-kosher birds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof from the next word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every צפור were kosher, the תורה would not need to say 'kosher birds.' Saying 'טהורות' suggests there are צפרים that are not kosher. That would contradict the view of רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter part (here, the end of the פסוק)
kosher (pure) ones
non-kosher (impure) ones

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter part: 'kosher,'
by inference, there are non-kosher ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'חיות' was explained away, the גמרא tries the next word of the same פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That some birds called צפור are non-kosher

steps.title: 'Kosher' excludes a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof. 'טהורות' excludes birds that are טריפות, not non-kosher species.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It implies there are טריפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying 'טהורות' is meant to exclude a different kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird can be from a kosher species but still be unfit because it is a טריפה. So 'טהורות' leaves out טריפות. It does not prove that non-kosher species are called צפור.

keyTerms.meaning: animals or birds with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even if from a kosher species

phrases.english: No. By inference, there are טריפות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of 'טהורות' as excluding non-kosher species
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'טהורות' can be excluding טריפות of a kosher species

steps.title: But a טריפה is already excluded by 'living'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 12. According to the view that a טריפה cannot live, the word 'חיות' already excludes it. Then 'טהורות' is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טריפה is already excluded by 'living.' That works well for the one who says a טריפה can live. But for the one who says a טריפה cannot live, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer that 'טהורות' comes to exclude a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute whether a טריפה can survive. If it can, it counts as 'living,' so we need 'טהורות' to exclude it. If it cannot survive, it is not 'living,' so 'חיות' already excludes it. Then 'טהורות' must be teaching something else, perhaps that non-kosher birds exist.

keyTerms.meaning: it is derived (from a source)
a טריפה can live (survive)
this works well (for one view)
what is there to say? (no good answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חיות' is being used in its plain sense, able to live. It is not 'permitted to eat,' which was the rejected reading in step 9.

phrases.english: טריפות are derived from 'living.'
phrases.notes: He means a bird that cannot survive does not count as 'living,' so it is already left out.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says a טריפה can live,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה אֵינָהּ חַיָּה,
phrases.english: but for the one who says a טריפה cannot live,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'טהורות' comes to exclude טריפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a טריפה cannot live, 'חיות' already excludes it, so 'טהורות' would add nothing

steps.title: According to everyone, a טריפה is excluded by another source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a stronger challenge. Whatever view one holds about a טריפה, it is already excluded by a teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: whether according to the one who says a טריפה can live, or according to the one who says it cannot live, it is derived from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the answer from step 12, and this one works according to both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a טריפה can live, we still do not need 'טהורות' to exclude it. A separate teaching already disqualifies it. So 'טהורות' again seems to have no job unless it points to non-kosher birds.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore; introduces an additional challenge

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה חַיָּה,
phrases.english: And furthermore, whether according to the one who says a טריפה can live,
or according to the one who says it cannot live,
it is derived from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 13 so that it works for both views.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'טהורות' comes to exclude טריפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל already excludes טריפות, so 'טהורות' is not needed for that under any view

steps.title: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the teaching it just mentioned. It compares offerings that 'enable' and 'atone' inside the בית המקדש with ones done outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: It says there are things that enable and things that atone inside, and it says there are things that enable and things that atone outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the source behind its challenge in step 14. This line sets up the comparison, and the teaching continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching sets up two parallel groups: offerings done inside the בית המקדש and procedures done outside it. Each group has something that enables a person and something that atones. This comparison will be used to show where the exclusion of a טריפה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: something that enables or makes fit, such as letting a person eat holy food
something that atones
inside (the בית המקדש)
outside (the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
It is stated that there is one that enables and one that atones inside,
phrases.notes: Inside means in the בית המקדש itself.

phrases.english: and it is stated that there is one that enables and one that atones outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source mentioned in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That טריפות are already excluded without the word 'טהורות'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל comparing what is done inside and outside the בית המקדש

steps.title: Offerings inside and outside the בית המקדש are compared
steps.stepSummary: The teaching concludes that an 'enabling' offering is treated like an 'atoning' one, both inside and outside the בית המקדש. So the מצורע's birds, like the שעיר המשתלח, may not be טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with the enabling and atoning offerings brought inside, the תורה treated the enabling offering like the atoning one, so too with the enabling and atoning offerings done outside, the תורה treated the enabling one like the atoning one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל. That teaching proves that the birds of a מצורע may not be טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the בית המקדש, the שעיר המשתלח atones and the מצורע's birds 'enable', meaning they make the person fit again. Since the enabler is treated like the atoner, the birds share the rule that a טריפה is unfit. So the word 'טהורות' is not needed to exclude a טריפה, and the answer from step 12 falls.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering or ritual that makes a person fit again (here, the מצורע's birds)
An offering that brings atonement (here, the שעיר המשתלח)
Inside, meaning offerings done in the בית המקדש
Outside, meaning rituals done outside the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the door on using 'טהורות' to exclude a טריפה. That forces the גמרא to look for a new meaning of the word.

phrases.english: Just as the enabling and the atoning offerings
that are stated inside [the Temple]
[the Torah] made the enabling one like the atoning one,
so too the enabling and the atoning ones
that are stated outside,
phrases.notes: Outside, the שעיר המשתלח is the one that atones, and the מצורע's birds are the ones that 'enable'.

phrases.english: [the Torah] made the enabling one like the atoning one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the teaching quoted in step 15, which supports the challenge in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a טריפה bird is already unfit for the מצורע's ritual without the word 'טהורות'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל, which compares offerings inside and outside the בית המקדש.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: excluding birds of a condemned city
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'טהורות' excludes birds from an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The word comes to exclude birds of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'טהורות' cannot be about a טריפה, רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the word a new job. It excludes birds from a city that turned to idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in an עיר הנדחת is forbidden for any benefit. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads 'טהורות' as making such birds unfit for the מצורע's ritual. This replaces the answer about טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people turned to idol worship. It is destroyed, and all its property is forbidden.
To exclude

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
[It comes] to exclude birds of a condemned city.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word 'טהורות' in the פסוק about the מצורע's birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading of 'טהורות' after the טריפה reading was knocked down.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'טהורות' excludes birds of an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: Which bird of the city is excluded?
steps.stepSummary: Birds of the condemned city are excluded for slaughter. For sending away they would be excluded anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If for sending away, the תורה would not say to send a bird out and create a stumbling block. Rather, it is for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which of the two birds this exclusion is about. It answers that it is the bird that gets slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forbidden bird could never be the one set free, because someone might catch and eat it. The תורה would not command something that leads people to sin, so no פסוק is needed for that. The new teaching must therefore be about the slaughtered bird.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? Which case does this teach?
Sending away: the live bird that is set free in the מצורע's ritual
A stumbling block, something that could lead people to sin
Slaughter: the other bird, which is slaughtered in the ritual

steps.confusionAlert: The מצורע's ritual uses two birds. One is slaughtered and one is sent away. Each 'למאי' asks which of these two birds the exclusion is talking about.

phrases.english: For what? If for sending away,
the Torah did not say
to send [a bird] out to become a stumbling block,
phrases.notes: If a forbidden bird is set free, someone could catch it and eat it without knowing.

phrases.english: rather, [it excludes it] for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies what רב נחמן בר יצחק's exclusion applies to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the exclusion apply to the bird that is sent away or to the bird that is slaughtered?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To the slaughtered bird. A forbidden bird is already unfit for sending, because the Torah would not cause a stumbling block.

steps.title: רבא: no pairing a bird before it is sent away
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'טהורות' teaches that a bird already used for one מצורע may not be paired for another before it is sent away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It comes to exclude, that one may not pair another bird with it before it has been sent away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different job for the word 'טהורות'. It forbids reusing a bird from one מצורע's ritual for another מצורע before that bird has been sent away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second, separate answer to what 'טהורות' excludes. It is about reusing a bird, not about where the bird came from.

keyTerms.meaning: To pair, matching one bird with another for the ritual
Before it has been sent away

phrases.english: Rava said: [It comes] to exclude,
that one may not pair another [bird] with it
phrases.notes: He means a bird already set aside for one מצורע, which someone wants to use again for a second מצורע.

phrases.english: before it has been sent away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְמַעוֹטֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְזַוֵּוג לָהּ אַחֶרֶת קוֹדֶם שִׁלּוּחֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רב נחמן בר יצחק about what 'טהורות' excludes.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'טהורות' forbids reusing a bird for another מצורע before it has been sent away.

steps.title: רבא's exclusion is about sending, not slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule cannot be about slaughter, because that bird still has to be sent away. It must mean that the bird cannot be sent for a second מצורע at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If for slaughter, this bird still needs to be sent away! Rather, it is about sending.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which bird רבא means. This time the answer is the bird that gets sent away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the first מצורע's bird for slaughter is obviously wrong, because that bird still has to be sent away for the first מצורע. So no verse is needed for that. The verse must teach that one bird cannot be sent away for two people at once.

keyTerms.meaning: But it requires, meaning it still needs something

steps.confusionAlert: Here the answer is the opposite of רב נחמן בר יצחק's. For רבא, the exclusion is about sending, not slaughter.

phrases.english: For what? If for slaughter,
it still needs to be sent away!
Rather, [it excludes it] for sending away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies what רבא's exclusion applies to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבא's exclusion apply to slaughter or to sending away?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To sending away. Slaughter is already ruled out, because the bird must still be sent away for the first מצורע.

steps.title: רב פפא: birds traded for idol-worship birds
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says 'טהורות' excludes birds received in exchange for birds of עבודה זרה, which are forbidden like the idol itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It excludes birds that someone exchanged for birds of עבודה זרה. As it is written, 'and you shall become accursed like it': whatever you produce from it is like it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third job for 'טהורות'. It excludes birds that were received in trade for idol-worship birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'והיית חרם כמהו' is read as a play on words: 'והיית' sounds like 'מהייה', to produce. So anything gained from an idol, even by trade, is forbidden just like the idol. Such birds are therefore unfit for the מצורע's ritual.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Something accursed and forbidden
Produce or generate, such as getting something by trading
That one exchanged them

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
[It excludes] birds that one exchanged
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'שהחליפו' (round brackets); the corrected wording is 'שהחליפן' (square brackets).

phrases.english: for birds of idol worship,
as it is written: 'and you shall become accursed like it,'
phrases.notes: דברים 7:26

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה מְהַיֶּיה הֵימֶנּוּ כָּמוֹהוּ.
phrases.english: anything you produce from it is like it.
phrases.notes: A play on words: 'והיית' (you shall become) is read like 'מהייה' (you produce).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְצִפֳּרִים שֶׁהֶחְלִיפָן בְּצִפֳּרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, alongside those of רב נחמן בר יצחק and רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative exclusion for the word, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'טהורות' excludes birds received in exchange for idol-worship birds.

steps.title: רב פפא's exclusion is about slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Exchanged idol birds are excluded for slaughter. For sending away they are excluded anyway, because they would be a stumbling block.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If for sending away, the תורה would not say to send a bird out and create a stumbling block. Rather, it is for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same 'for what?' question about רב פפא's case. It gives the same answer it gave for the condemned city: slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exchanged idol birds are forbidden, so they could never be set free. Someone might eat them, and the תורה would not cause that. So 'טהורות' must teach that they are unfit as the slaughtered bird.

keyTerms.meaning: If
Rather

phrases.english: For what? If for sending away,
the Torah did not say to send [a bird] out to become a stumbling block,
rather, [it excludes it] for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies what רב פפא's exclusion applies to, using the same reasoning as step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב פפא's exclusion apply to sending away or to slaughter?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To slaughter. Sending away is already ruled out because of the stumbling-block principle.

steps.title: רבינא: a bird that killed a person
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a new answer: the word טהורות excludes a bird that killed a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: What case are we dealing with here? A bird that killed a person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a fourth answer for what the word טהורות comes to exclude: a bird that killed a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird that kills a person is subject to being put to death by a court. רבינא suggests the פסוק is teaching that such a bird cannot be used for the מצורע's ritual. The גמרא will now test exactly when and how this exclusion works.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a way of setting up a specific case)
A bird that killed a person

phrases.english: Ravina said: Here, what are we dealing with?
With a bird that killed a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer for what 'טהורות' excludes, alongside those of רב נחמן בר יצחק, רבא and רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case definition for what the פסוק excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טהורות' excludes a טריפה bird, but that exclusion is already known from other sources.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exclusion is about a bird that killed a person.

steps.title: Before or after the verdict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when this bird is being judged and concludes it must be before its verdict.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If its verdict was already given, it is already condemned to death! Rather, it is before its verdict was given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבינא's answer by asking at what stage this bird is. If it was already sentenced, no פסוק is needed, so it must be before the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a court sentences the bird, it is obviously set to be killed, so the פסוק would teach nothing new. That pushes the case back to before the sentence, when the bird is guilty but not yet condemned. The גמרא now has a case where a פסוק could teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact facts?
The final verdict of its trial
Subject to being put to death

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If its verdict was issued –
It is subject to being killed!
Rather, it is before its verdict was issued,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down רבינא's case to a specific stage of the trial.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what stage of judgment is the bird that killed a person?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before its verdict, since after the verdict no פסוק is needed.

steps.title: Excluded for slaughter, not for sending away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which use is excluded and concludes the פסוק disqualifies this bird for slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what is it excluded? If for sending away — you must bring it to court to fulfill 'and you shall remove the evil from your midst'! Rather, it is for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: Following the same pattern as before, the גמרא asks whether the exclusion is for the bird that is slaughtered or the one that is sent away. It concludes: for slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You obviously cannot set free a bird that must stand trial, because the תורה requires bringing it to court and removing the evil. So no פסוק is needed for sending away. The פסוק must be teaching that this bird cannot be the one slaughtered, which is something we would not have known otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Sending away (here, the live bird set free in the מצורע's ritual)
Slaughter (the bird that is slaughtered in the ritual)
'And you shall remove the evil from your midst'

steps.whatToRemember: There are four answers for what 'טהורות' excludes. רב נחמן בר יצחק says birds of an עיר הנדחת, for slaughter. רבא says pairing a bird before it is sent away, for sending. רב פפא says birds exchanged for idol birds, for slaughter. רבינא says a bird that killed a person, before its verdict, for slaughter.

phrases.english: And for what?
phrases.notes: For which of the two birds in the ritual: the one slaughtered or the one sent away?

phrases.english: If for sending away –
One must bring it to the court
And fulfill 'And you shall eradicate the evil from your midst'!
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6

phrases.english: Rather, it is for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes testing רבינא's case by identifying which use is excluded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the bird excluded from sending away or from slaughter?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From slaughter, since sending it away is already forbidden because it must be brought to court.

steps.title: The משנה: a non-kosher bird on kosher eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה: a non-kosher bird sitting on a kosher bird's eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher bird resting on the eggs of a kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, quoting a line from the משנה about שילוח הקן. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a non-kosher bird sits on kosher eggs, or a kosher bird sits on non-kosher eggs, there is no מצוה to send away the mother. The גמרא quotes the first half to begin discussing both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird
A kosher bird
Sitting / resting (on the nest)

phrases.english: A non-kosher bird resting
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, which also has the opposite case and says both are exempt from sending away.

phrases.english: On the eggs of a kosher bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹף טָמֵא רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי עוֹף טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of the מצורע's birds and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the bird and the eggs do not match in kosher status, there is no מצוה of שילוח הקן.

steps.title: But a kosher bird on non-kosher eggs is a צפור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the first case but challenges the second: the mother there is a kosher bird, so why no מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that a non-kosher bird on kosher eggs is exempt — we need a 'צפור' and there isn't one. But a kosher bird on non-kosher eggs — that is a 'צפור'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the משנה. If the mother is a kosher bird, why is there no מצוה to send it away?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צפור in the פסוק was earlier explained to mean a kosher bird. A non-kosher mother is not a צפור, so the exemption makes sense. But when the mother is kosher, the requirement of צפור is met, so the exemption needs a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (accepting one part before challenging another)
Bird; here understood as a kosher bird
And it is not there

phrases.english: Granted, a non-kosher bird resting
On the eggs of a kosher bird –
We require a 'tzippor' and there is none,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:6. Earlier the גמרא learned that צפור means a kosher bird.

phrases.english: But a kosher bird resting
On the eggs of a non-kosher bird –
It is a 'tzippor'!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא עוֹף טָמֵא רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second case of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's exemption of a kosher bird sitting on non-kosher eggs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only reason given so far is that the mother must be a צפור (kosher), and here she is kosher.

steps.title: 'Take for yourself' — not for your dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב כהנא's rule: the young must be fit for you to eat, not just for your dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב כהנא said: 'You may take for yourself' — and not for your dogs. Here too: 'You may take for yourself' — and not for your dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by borrowing a teaching of רב כהנא. Non-kosher eggs are only good for dogs, so there is no מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'and the young you may take for yourself', which shows the מצוה applies only when the young are something you yourself can eat. Non-kosher eggs cannot be eaten by a Jew, so even though the mother is kosher, there is no שילוח הקן. The exemption now comes from the eggs, not from the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You may take for yourself' (דברים 22:7)
And not for your dogs
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate requirements: the mother must be a kosher צפור, and the young must be fit for you to eat. Either one missing means no מצוה.

phrases.english: As Rav Kahana said:
'You may take for yourself' – and not for your dogs,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:7

phrases.english: Here too:
'You may take for yourself' – and not for your dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a known teaching from another context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the mother is a kosher צפור, the מצוה should apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The young must also be fit for you to eat; non-kosher eggs are only 'for your dogs', so there is no מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the מצוה of שילוח הקן depends on the young being permitted to eat, not only on the mother.

steps.title: Where was רב כהנא's teaching first said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what original context רב כהנא said his teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רב כהנא's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא used רב כהנא's teaching 'like he said', it now asks where he originally said it. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'as רב כהנא said' points to an earlier source. The גמרא wants to show the original case so we understand the teaching properly.

keyTerms.meaning: And where was it stated?

phrases.english: And where was the statement of Rav Kahana stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the source of the teaching just used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רב כהנא's teaching.

steps.title: The ברייתא: טרפה mother and טרפה chicks
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it was said on a ברייתא that says a טרפה mother must be sent away, but טרפה chicks exempt you.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what was taught: If the mother is a טרפה, one must send her away. If the chicks are טרפות, one is exempt from sending away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא's teaching was said on a ברייתא about טרפה birds. First it quotes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a surprising split. A טרפה mother still requires sending away, but if the chicks are טרפות, there is no מצוה at all. The next step gives the source for the chicks' exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
Chicks / fledglings
Exempt
Obligated

phrases.english: On that which was taught in a baraita:
A mother that is a tereifa – one is obligated to send her away,
Chicks that are tereifot – one is exempt from sending away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 by naming the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב כהנא's teaching was said on the ברייתא about a טרפה mother and טרפה chicks.

steps.title: Source for the ברייתא: 'take for yourself'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule, and רב כהנא answers: 'You may take for yourself' — not for your dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this? רב כהנא said: Because the פסוק says 'You may take for yourself' — and not for your dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's rule about טרפה chicks comes from, and here is רב כהנא's original teaching. This closes the loop on the teaching used in step 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טרפה chicks cannot be eaten by a Jew, so they are only fit for dogs. Since the פסוק says the young are 'for yourself', the מצוה applies only when they can be eaten. The same reasoning explains why non-kosher eggs exempt you as well.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The mother's status alone does not decide the מצוה: if the young are not fit for you to eat (non-kosher eggs or טרפה chicks), there is no שילוח הקן, based on 'תקח לך – ולא לכלביך'.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
Rav Kahana said:
As the verse states: 'You may take for yourself' –
And not for your dogs.
phrases.notes: טרפה chicks can only be given to dogs, so they don't count as 'for yourself'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ברייתא quoted in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for exempting טרפה chicks.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'תקח לך' teaches that the young must be fit for you, not for your dogs.

steps.title: Why not compare a טרפה mother to טרפה chicks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: since טרפה chicks exempt you from שילוח הקן, a טרפה mother should exempt you too, by comparing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not compare a טרפה mother to the chicks? Just as with טרפה chicks you are exempt from sending away the mother, so too with a טרפה mother you should also be exempt from sending her away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 30, which said a טרפה mother must still be sent away. It asks why we don't treat the mother the same way as the chicks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא showed from 'You may take for yourself' that טרפה chicks exempt you, since they are not fit for you to eat. The גמרא now suggests a comparison (היקש): mother and chicks are both in the same פסוק, so a טרפה mother should exempt you just like טרפה chicks do. That would contradict the ברייתא's first ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: to compare two things that the תורה links together, giving them the same law
a mother bird with a fatal defect, which makes it not kosher to eat
chicks, young birds
sending away the mother bird (the מצוה of שילוח הקן)
exempt, not obligated

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא said the opposite: a טרפה mother must still be sent away. The גמרא is not ruling here, only pushing on the ברייתא to see why it does not compare the two.

phrases.english: But let us compare a טרפה mother to the chicks,
just as with טרפה chicks, one is exempt from sending away,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵם טְרֵפָה נָמֵי – פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּחַ.
phrases.english: so too with a טרפה mother, one should also be exempt from sending away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's first ruling (a טרפה mother must be sent away) by using רב כהנא's derivation about טרפה chicks from Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a טרפה mother must still be sent away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mother and chicks are linked in the same פסוק, so they should share a law. Since טרפה chicks exempt you, a טרפה mother should exempt you too.
